bottom_line: Aducanumab — ENGAGE / EMERGE. Stated failure: Phase III: both stopped for futility; fuller data later positive in EMERGE, negative in ENGAGE. Mixed/reversed case. Diagnosis (claim 1.3, supported): In ENGAGE, neither aducanumab dose separated from placebo on CDR-SB: low dose difference 0.11 (95% CI -0.469 to 0.403, p=0.225); high dose difference 0.03 (95% CI -0.262 to 0.326, p=0.833).
lines: [1] Both phase III studies ENGAGE and EMERGE stopped after an interim futility analysis. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: mixed: some records support it, some do not).

[2] The prespecified primary endpoint for both trials was change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 78. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: mixed: some records support it, some do not).

[3] In ENGAGE, neither aducanumab dose separated from placebo on CDR-SB: low dose difference 0.11 (95% CI -0.469 to 0.403, p=0.225); high dose difference 0.03 (95% CI -0.262 to 0.326, p=0.833). (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[4] In EMERGE, the high-dose group showed a statistically significant CDR-SB benefit versus placebo (-0.39, 95% CI -0.694 to -0.086, p=0.012), while the low-dose group did not (-0.26, 95% CI -0.569 to 0.041, p=0.0901). [5] A larger data cut made EMERGE positive; exposure-related analyses were offered to explain discordant ENGAGE results. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[6] Biogen reversed the abandonment decision and submitted for approval; accelerated US approval followed in 2021 based on amyloid reduction, and Biogen discontinued development/commercialization in 2024. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[7] In EMERGE, the primary CDR-SB Week 78 result for the higher-dose group versus placebo was -0.39 (95% CI -0.694 to -0.086, p=0.012), while the lower-dose group was -0.26 (95% CI -0.569 to 0.041, p=0.0901). (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[8] In ENGAGE, the primary CDR-SB Week 78 result for the higher-dose group versus placebo was 0.11 (95% CI -0.469 to 0.403, p=0.225), and versus the late-start group was 0.03 (95% CI -0.262 to 0.326, p=0.833). (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[9] ENGAGE (NCT02477800) tested aducanumab in Alzheimer disease. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[10] EMERGE (NCT02484547) studied aducanumab in Alzheimer disease. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[11] Aducanumab interacts with amyloid-beta precursor protein. (section: Related Indications; sources: ChEMBL; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[12] ENGAGE (NCT02477800) studies Alzheimer Disease and tests ADUCANUMAB; EMERGE (NCT02484547) studies Alzheimer Disease; the Aducanumab ENGAGE/EMERGE program has intervention ADUCANUMAB. [13] In EMERGE, the primary CDR-SB change at Week 78 showed a difference vs placebo of -0.26 (p=0.0901) for one dose and -0.39 (p=0.012) for the higher dose, indicating a nominally significant benefit only at the higher dose. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[15] EMERGE secondary ADCS-ADL-MCI results were 0.7 (p=0.1515) and 1.7 (p=0.0006) vs placebo, while ENGAGE ADCS-ADL-MCI results were 0.7 (p=0.1225) and 0.7 (p=0.1506), neither significant. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

(section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

question: Why were aducanumab's ENGAGE and EMERGE trials stopped for futility, and what did the fuller data show?
raw: Both phase III trials were stopped after an interim futility analysis [1], a curated summary rather than a direct statistical result. The prespecified primary endpoint was change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 78 [2]. In ENGAGE, neither dose separated from placebo: low dose difference 0.11 (95% CI -0.469 to 0.403, p=0.225); high dose difference 0.03 (95% CI -0.262 to 0.326, p=0.833) [3,8]. In EMERGE, the high-dose group showed a statistically significant benefit versus placebo (-0.39, 95% CI -0.694 to -0.086, p=0.012), while the low-dose group did not (-0.26, 95% CI -0.569 to 0.041, p=0.0901) [4,7,13]. A larger data cut made EMERGE positive, and exposure-related analyses were offered to explain discordant ENGAGE results [5,17], though the lines do not show the underlying exposure data or causal mechanisms. Biogen later reversed the abandonment decision and submitted for approval [6,17].
